## Built-in themes

ggplot2 ships with 8 themes. The default is `theme_grey()` — you never need to specify it unless you want to be explicit.

```r
install.packages("ggplot2")
library(ggplot2)
```

| Function | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `theme_grey()` | Default — grey background, white grid lines |
| `theme_bw()` | Black & white — white panel, dark border |
| `theme_linedraw()` | Black lines on white background only |
| `theme_light()` | Like linedraw but with grey lines and axes |
| `theme_dark()` | Dark panel background |
| `theme_minimal()` | No background annotations — very clean |
| `theme_classic()` | No grid lines — axes only |
| `theme_void()` | Completely empty — blank canvas |

### Examples

```r
library(ggplot2)
iris -> dataset

p <- ggplot(dataset, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~ Species)

p + theme_grey()      # default
p + theme_bw(base_size = 14)
p + theme_minimal()
p + theme_classic()
p + theme_dark()
p + theme_light()
p + theme_linedraw()
p + theme_void()
```

::: {.callout-tip}
## `base_size` argument
All built-in themes accept a `base_size` argument to scale all text proportionally:

```r
p + theme_bw(base_size = 20)   # larger text
p + theme_minimal(base_size = 9) # smaller text
```
:::

## ggthemes

`ggthemes` contains themes inspired by well-known publications and tools. Many come with matching colour scales.

```r
install.packages("ggthemes")
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)
```

### Available themes

```r
theme_base()            theme_calc()
theme_clean()           theme_economist()
theme_excel()           theme_excel_new()
theme_few()             theme_fivethirtyeight()
theme_foundation()      theme_gdocs()
theme_hc()              theme_igray()
theme_map()             theme_pander()
theme_solarized()       theme_solid()
theme_stata()           theme_tufte()
theme_wsj()
```

### Usage examples

```r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggthemes)

cyls <- as.factor(mtcars$cyl)
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, fill = cyls)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.7) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

# The Economist style
p + theme_economist() + scale_fill_economist()

# FiveThirtyEight style
p + theme_fivethirtyeight() + scale_fill_fivethirtyeight()

# Wall Street Journal
p + theme_wsj() + scale_fill_wsj()

# Stata
p + theme_stata() + scale_color_stata()

# Edward Tufte minimalism
p + theme_tufte()

# Google Docs
p + theme_gdocs() + scale_fill_gdocs()

# Excel (new)
p + theme_excel_new() + scale_fill_excel_new()

# Stephen Few
p + theme_few() + scale_fill_few()

# Highcharts
p + theme_hc() + scale_fill_hc()

# Base R look
p + theme_base()

# Solarized
p + theme_solarized() + scale_fill_solarized()
```

### Matching colour scales

| Theme | Colour scale |
|-------|-------------|
| `theme_economist()` | `scale_colour_economist()` / `scale_fill_economist()` |
| `theme_fivethirtyeight()` | `scale_colour_fivethirtyeight()` |
| `theme_wsj()` | `scale_colour_wsj()` / `scale_fill_wsj()` |
| `theme_stata()` | `scale_colour_stata()` |
| `theme_gdocs()` | `scale_fill_gdocs()` |
| `theme_few()` | `scale_colour_few()` / `scale_fill_few()` |
| `theme_hc()` | `scale_colour_hc()` / `scale_fill_hc()` |
| `theme_solarized()` | `scale_colour_solarized()` / `scale_fill_solarized()` |

## hrbrthemes

`hrbrthemes` provides **typography-centric** themes — clean, minimal, with beautiful font choices.

```r
install.packages("hrbrthemes")
library(ggplot2)
library(hrbrthemes)
```

### Available themes

```r
theme_ipsum()         # Arial Narrow
theme_ipsum_es()      # Esteban
theme_ipsum_rc()      # Roboto Condensed
theme_ipsum_ps()      # IBM Plex Sans
theme_ipsum_pub()     # Public Sans
theme_ipsum_tw()      # Titillium Web
theme_ipsum_modern_rc() # Modern Roboto Condensed dark
theme_ft_rc()         # Roboto Condensed (FT-inspired)
theme_modern_rc()     # Dark Roboto Condensed
theme_tinyhand()
```

### Usage examples

```r
library(ggplot2)
library(hrbrthemes)

iris -> dataset

p <- ggplot(dataset, aes(x = Sepal.Length, y = Sepal.Width, fill = Species)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  facet_wrap(~ Species)

# Arial Narrow
p + theme_ipsum() + theme(legend.position = "top")

# Roboto Condensed
p + theme_ipsum_rc() + theme(legend.position = "top")

# FT-inspired dark
p + theme_ft_rc() + theme(legend.position = "top")

# With matching scale
p + theme_ipsum() + scale_fill_ipsum() +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

## ggdark

`ggdark` provides **dark mode** versions of all 8 built-in ggplot2 themes. It can also convert **any** theme into dark mode with `dark_mode()`.

```r
install.packages("ggdark")
library(ggplot2)
library(ggdark)
```

### Dark theme functions

```r
dark_theme_gray()       dark_theme_bw()
dark_theme_linedraw()   dark_theme_light()
dark_theme_dark()       dark_theme_minimal()
dark_theme_classic()    dark_theme_void()

# Convert any theme to dark mode
dark_mode(theme_economist())
dark_mode(theme_ipsum())
```

### Usage examples

```r
library(ggplot2)
library(ggdark)

mtcars -> dt
cyls <- as.factor(dt$cyl)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, fill = cyls)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.7) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

p + dark_theme_classic()
p + dark_theme_linedraw()
p + dark_theme_minimal()

# Dark mode on any theme
p + dark_mode(theme_minimal())
p + dark_mode(theme_economist())
```

## mdthemes

`mdthemes` wraps all themes from ggplot2, ggthemes, hrbrthemes and other packages with **Markdown support** — plot titles and labels can use `**bold**` and `*italic*` syntax.

```r
install.packages("mdthemes")
library(ggplot2)
library(mdthemes)
```

```r
library(ggplot2)
library(mdthemes)

cyls <- as.factor(mtcars$cyl)

p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, fill = cyls)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.7) +
  labs(title    = "**Fuel Economy** by *Cylinders*",
       subtitle = "**Bold** and *italic* in titles") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

# Regular theme — markdown NOT rendered
p + theme_bw()

# md version — markdown IS rendered
p + md_theme_bw()
p + md_theme_minimal()
p + md_theme_classic()
```

## ggthemr

`ggthemr` works differently — it sets a **global theme** for all subsequent plots using `ggthemr()`, rather than being added as a layer.

```r
# Install from GitHub
# devtools::install_github('Mikata-Project/ggthemr')
library(ggthemr)
library(ggplot2)
```

```r
# Set a global theme
ggthemr("flat")

cyls <- as.factor(mtcars$cyl)
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, fill = cyls)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.7) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")

# ALWAYS reset after use
ggthemr_reset()
```

### Available palettes

```r
ggthemr("flat")           ggthemr("flat dark")
ggthemr("camouflage")     ggthemr("carrot")
ggthemr("chalk")          ggthemr("copper")
ggthemr("dust")           ggthemr("earth")
ggthemr("fresh")          ggthemr("grape")
ggthemr("grass")          ggthemr("greyscale")
ggthemr("light")          ggthemr("lilac")
ggthemr("pale")           ggthemr("sea")
ggthemr("sky")            ggthemr("solarized")
```

::: {.callout-warning}
## Always reset ggthemr
ggthemr sets a global state. Always call `ggthemr_reset()` when done to restore the default ggplot2 theme.
:::

## ggtech

`ggtech` provides themes inspired by major tech companies.

```r
# Install from GitHub
# devtools::install_github("ricardo-bion/ggtech", dependencies = TRUE)
library(ggtech)
library(ggplot2)
```

```r
cyls <- as.factor(mtcars$cyl)

ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = mpg, fill = cyls)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.7) +
  ggtitle("Tech company themes") +
  theme_tech(theme = "airbnb") +
  scale_fill_tech(theme = "airbnb") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

### Available styles

```r
theme_tech(theme = "airbnb")    # Airbnb coral & grey
theme_tech(theme = "google")    # Google colours
theme_tech(theme = "twitter")   # Twitter blue
theme_tech(theme = "facebook")  # Facebook blue
theme_tech(theme = "etsy")      # Etsy orange
theme_tech(theme = "X23andme")  # 23andMe
```

## Setting a global theme

Use `theme_set()` to apply a theme to **all subsequent plots** in your session:

```r
library(ggplot2)

# Save current theme and set a new one
old <- theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 13))

# Now ALL plots use theme_minimal
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg)) + geom_point()
ggplot(iris, aes(x = Sepal.Width)) + geom_histogram()

# Restore the previous theme
theme_set(old)
```

## Custom theme with `theme()`

Build your own reusable theme:

```r
library(ggplot2)

my_theme <- theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    # Titles
    plot.title      = element_text(face = "bold", size = 16,
                                   colour = "#0e0f14", margin = margin(b = 8)),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(colour = "#6b6760", size = 12,
                                   margin = margin(b = 12)),
    plot.caption    = element_text(colour = "#aaaaaa", size = 9, hjust = 1),

    # Axes
    axis.title      = element_text(size = 11, colour = "#3d3e47"),
    axis.text       = element_text(size = 10, colour = "#6b6760"),
    axis.line       = element_line(colour = "#d8d2c8"),

    # Grid
    panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#ede8df", linewidth = 0.4),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#faf8f4", colour = NA),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "#ffffff", colour = NA),

    # Legend
    legend.position  = "top",
    legend.title     = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
    legend.text      = element_text(size = 10),

    # Facet strips
    strip.background = element_blank(),
    strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", size = 11),

    # Margins
    plot.margin      = margin(16, 16, 16, 16)
  )

# Apply to any plot
ggplot(mtcars, aes(x = wt, y = mpg, colour = factor(cyl))) +
  geom_point(size = 3, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#e84855","#2d6be4","#12a36a")) +
  labs(title = "Custom Theme", colour = "Cylinders") +
  my_theme
```

---

## Quick reference — theme() arguments

| Argument | Controls | Function |
|----------|---------|---------|
| `plot.title` | Title text | `element_text()` |
| `plot.subtitle` | Subtitle text | `element_text()` |
| `plot.caption` | Caption text | `element_text()` |
| `plot.background` | Outer plot area | `element_rect()` |
| `panel.background` | Inner panel area | `element_rect()` |
| `panel.grid.major` | Major grid lines | `element_line()` / `element_blank()` |
| `panel.grid.minor` | Minor grid lines | `element_line()` / `element_blank()` |
| `panel.border` | Panel border | `element_rect()` |
| `axis.title` | Axis label text | `element_text()` |
| `axis.text` | Axis tick labels | `element_text()` |
| `axis.text.x` | X-axis tick labels | `element_text(angle = 45)` |
| `axis.line` | Axis lines | `element_line()` |
| `axis.ticks` | Tick marks | `element_line()` / `element_blank()` |
| `legend.position` | Legend location | `"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"none"`, `c(x,y)` |
| `legend.title` | Legend title text | `element_text()` |
| `legend.background` | Legend background | `element_rect()` |
| `legend.key.size` | Legend key size | `unit(1, "cm")` |
| `strip.background` | Facet strip bg | `element_rect()` / `element_blank()` |
| `strip.text` | Facet strip text | `element_text()` |
| `plot.margin` | Outer margins | `margin(t, r, b, l)` |
